one-illness-away.name: Medical bills
one-illness-away.line: One bad illness could wipe out everything I have.
one-illness-away.why: Brings back what the ID names, the fear of being one illness from ruin, instead of a general worry about cost, which also keeps it apart from personal Healthcare (getting care at all).

one-illness-away.name: Cost of illness

one-illness-away.why: Uses the earlier alias people recognized, and a name that says the problem rather than the paperwork.

mental-health-crisis.name: Mental health crisis

mental-health-crisis.why: Keeps the line and makes the name a problem label, so the Health heading no longer mixes areas and problems.

mental-health-crisis.name: People not okay
mental-health-crisis.line: So many people around me aren't okay.
mental-health-crisis.why: The earlier alias, said the way people say it out loud; a problem label that fits the rest of the heading.

older-people-alone.name: Older people alone
older-people-alone.line: I see older people left on their own.
older-people-alone.why: Keeps the line and names the problem the ID describes; "Aging" is an area and reads like a personal worry about getting old.

older-people-alone.name: Growing old alone
older-people-alone.line: Older people around me are left to cope on their own.
older-people-alone.why: The earlier alias as the name, and a line that says plainly who is left and what that means.

pairs.reason: Being ruined by medical bills is a shared problem with how care is paid for, while not being able to see a doctor is a personal problem of getting care at all, so both belong, linked across pages.
Having no savings for any surprise bill is personal, while fearing that illness itself could ruin you points at how healthcare is paid for, so keep both and link them.
Feeling low yourself and seeing people around you struggle are different things to pick, one personal and one shared, so keep both linked across pages.
Worrying too much yourself is a personal pain, while watching people you care about struggle is a shared one, so keep both linked across pages.
Not being able to stop something yourself is a personal pain, while losing people you know to drugs is a shared one, so keep both linked across pages.
Feeling alone yourself is personal, while seeing older people left on their own is a shared problem, so keep both linked across pages.
Looking after someone yourself is a personal load, while older people left without anyone is a shared problem, so keep both linked across pages.

pairs.distinction: One is about people struggling with their mental health, the other about losing people to drugs; someone can tell them apart at a glance.
pairs.reason: They often go together, but someone watching friends struggle and someone losing friends to drugs would each know which one is theirs.

pairs.distinction: Education is about what kids get at school today; Kids' future is the broader worry that their whole lives will be harder than ours.
pairs.reason: Someone upset about their local school and someone dreading the world kids will inherit are naming different things, and a person can pick between them without thinking twice.

pairs.distinction: Kids' future compares one generation with the last; Opportunity compares people born in different places or families at the same time.
pairs.reason: Worrying that every kid will have it worse is not the same complaint as seeing some kids held back by where they started.

pairs.distinction: Climate change is one specific cause; Kids' future also covers costs, jobs, housing and the general sense that things are going backward.
pairs.reason: Many people who fear kids will have it worse are thinking about money and housing rather than the planet, so folding this into climate would lose them.
Losing my own nights to my phone is a personal pain while phones shaping a whole generation of kids is a societal one, so each belongs on its own page with a link between them.

world-on-fire.name: War
world-on-fire.line: I'm scared that war will reach people and places I care about.
world-on-fire.why: Keeps the plain name and the people and places I care about, but says the feeling out loud the way a person would, instead of the stiffer "I see war threatening".

world-on-fire.name: War and conflict
world-on-fire.line: I'm afraid the wars and conflicts in the world keep getting closer to home.
world-on-fire.why: Brings back the wider sense the ID names (war and chaos spreading, from the earlier line "War and chaos feel closer every year") while staying one plain worry.

crime-and-violence.name: Crime
crime-and-violence.line: Crime and violence keep hurting people in my community.
crime-and-violence.why: Makes this the shared, societal pain (people getting hurt around me) so it reads differently from the personal "I don't feel safe where I live", using the earlier alias's idea that it keeps happening.

pairs.distinction: Crime is violence between people where I live and in my country; War is armed conflict between countries or groups, often far away but reaching people I care about.
pairs.reason: Someone worried about break-ins and shootings on their street and someone worried about wars abroad are telling different stories, and nobody would hesitate between the two.

pairs.distinction: Safety on the personal page is my own sense of safety at home and on my street; Crime on the societal page is crime and violence as a problem we share.
pairs.reason: Feeling unsafe where I live is the personal side of the same worry as crime in society, so both pages should keep their own pain, linked across pages.

data.notes: Twenty lists read, 105 entries. oecd.org returned 403 (How's Life chapter), so OECD entries are the Health dimension from the OECD slide deck on unstats.un.org, the Better Life Index health indicators from Wikipedia, and deaths of despair from a healthpopuli summary of How's Life 2024. The Ipsos Health Service Report 2025 PDF gave two ranked lists (health problems; health-system problems) with 30-country averages; its text was extracted with a small zlib script because WebFetch could not read the PDF. The Gallup MIP page loaded without its table, so only the Healthcare category (named in the money sweep) is listed. The national 211 snapshot names only mental health and substance use among health needs; Michigan, New Jersey and Ontario 211 reports failed to load or parse. medicine-shortages stays a draft: ASHP's statistics page returned 403. data.notes: Seventeen lists read. The Kids group had only three pains, so most entries had no cover; 11 candidates proposed, all with opened sources. oecd.org (including the Child Well-being Dashboard) and its cedefop mirror returned 403, so OECD entries come from the OECD slides mirrored on unstats.un.org. WHOQOL-BREF and Gallup's five elements have no item about children (adult instruments), so they have no entries here. The 211 national snapshot gives no child-specific need, only 'family support' (#5). The newest Pew school-shooting survey that would open is from 2018; the CDC YRBS 2023 figures back the same candidate. Pew's 2024 school-shooting page returned 403. Gallup MIP figures come from the Datawrapper table vEKjO on the page (latest column 26-Sep). Wikidata QIDs were found with the wbsearchentities API (rate-limited, retried; not counted as searches). Overlaps for refine: childcare-shortage vs childcare-costs (availability vs cost); kids-mental-health vs mental-health-crisis; child-poverty vs poverty; guns-and-kids vs crime-and-violence; kids-unsafe-online vs screens-and-kids; moms-and-babies may fit Health better than Kids; child-abuse vs unsafe-at-home (personal). child-abuse and kids-unsafe-online are tagged sensitive. data.notes: Nineteen lists read. oecd.org returned 403, so OECD Safety indicators come from the public Better Life Index mirror (oecd-better-life-index.truth-and-beauty.net). The Ipsos PDF and Pew topline were read with a local PDF text extractor; Gallup tables were read from the page HTML. Wikidata QIDs came from the wbsearchentities API (22 lookups, not counted as searches). Coverage is low on most lists because nine candidates are waiting for review; once accepted, most lists pass 90%. Remaining gaps are outOfScope or broader on purpose: work safety (work sweep proposes unsafe-work), drinking water (home sweep proposes tap-water), suicide (mind sweep proposes suicidal-thoughts), politics as a safety risk (government sweep proposes political-violence), falls and drowning (personal injury; the founder pool lead 'I worry about what would happen if I fell or had an emergency while alone' could become a Body or Home pain), and pandemics (SDG 3.d, Health group). Likely twins for review: terrorism vs government/political-violence; school-shootings overlaps gun-violence and could sit under Kids; violence-against-women overlaps unsafe-at-home (personal) as the societal view; elder-abuse overlaps older-people-alone. CDC FastStats figures are the latest year shown on the page; the year isn't quoted, so prevalence says 'the latest year of CDC data'. child-abuse was removed from this run's candidates at the coordinator's request because the kids sweep 20261019-230115 proposes the same ID; its 4 list entries are marked outOfScope. Sources it relied on: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/child-maltreatment ("One in 5 women and 1 in 7 men report having been sexually abused as a child.", accessed 2026-10-19); https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/child-maltreatment ("Six in 10 children – or 400 million children – under 5 years of age regularly suffer physical punishment", accessed 2026-10-19). Prevalence as drafted: 1 in 5 women and 1 in 7 men report having been sexually abused as a child; 400 million children under 5 regularly suffer physical punishment or psychological violence at home (WHO).
